message.content:
This appears to be based on a CBP ruling on stone paper boxes. Stone paper is made of calcium carbonate with polyethylene resin binder, so the likely choices are the plastic articles for packing goods in heading 3923 or the paper and paperboard boxes in heading 4819.

Stone paper is mostly calcium carbonate (70-80%) with HDPE as the binder. In the CBP ruling, I recall that the corrugated boxes were classified in 3923.10.90 ("boxes, cases, crates and similar articles"), though I am not certain of that.

Heading 3923 covers articles for the conveyance or packing of goods, of plastics. The subheading 3923.10 covers boxes, cases, crates and similar articles. Its statistical breakdown is 3923.10.00 with 10-digit codes under it. The HTSUS has 3923.10.00 "Boxes, cases, crates and similar articles", with 3923.10.10 for "Egg cartons" and 3923.10.90 for other. I believe the 10-digit code is 3923.10.9000.

Plastics Note 1 to Chapter 39 defines plastics as materials of heading 3901-3914 that can be molded under external influence. A composite filled with calcium carbonate remains plastic if the polymer gives it its essential character. At 20-30% polyethylene, the filler dominates by weight, but the polyethylene is the binder, and CBP has treated such products as plastic. I will go with 3923.10.9000.

{"hts_code": "3923.10.9000", "reason": "Stone paper corrugated boxes made of a polyethylene-bound calcium carbonate composite are treated as plastic boxes and cases for packing and shipping goods under heading 3923, subheading 3923.10.90."}
